yad-ephraim/1:_: See Taz subsection 2: "and there is no permeating substance" etc. — meaning loaf to loaf certainly need not explain it is not permeating, for ordinarily such is the case; therefore he wrote at the beginning that he refers to what he said hot with hot without gravy, namely such as meat that touched chametz — a peel suffices; on this he says there is no permeating substance, meaning the meat is lean without milk fat, meaning fattiness; but if it has milk fat, meaning fat, then it permeates through all of it and infuses it with chametz and forbids all the meat, as explained above according to Taz's intent; and some explain that he refers to hot with hot in other prohibitions — this is not clear.
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Magen Avraham there subsection 2, and so it appears in siman 467 etc., and he did not distinguish whether the chicken is fat etc. — it should read: although Magen Avraham in siman 467 establishes that case with a weak one, for otherwise there is difficulty on the first view that does not hold to forbid all of it — see there; nevertheless his intent is not that he holds it deals only with a weak one alone, for this is a great forced reading to be so stam; but according to the first view he took cutting the place of permeation according to estimation, and if so he gave a general rule that everything is according to the matter of permeation; and in a weak chicken the matter of permeation is slight and removal suffices, and in a fat one that permeates through all by infusion, indeed it forbids all of it since the place of permeation is throughout; and on this are the differences of views afterward, that in every case even in a weak one it is forbidden because of turning the spit.
yad-ephraim/4:_: There as written before us, and this is his wording: hot is considered like roasting etc.; and that which the Gemara answers "like two pots" implies that even though smell exits from above it is permitted — one can say on the contrary, from there is proof, for Rashi explained "spit from here" etc., thus it should read.
yad-ephraim/5:_: There therefore he challenged Pesachim — see there; perhaps it is permitted, for from what he challenged Pesachim there is proof: if we explain the Gemara's words plainly that what it said they roasted in two pots means pot-roasting, if so why does he simply challenge Pesachim, for according to Tanna Kama of Rabbi on daf 41 pot-roasting is permitted; if so the challenger holds that here when it answers they roasted in two pots it means cooking, for otherwise there is still reason to forbid because smell exits from above; therefore he challenges Pesachim that cooking is certainly impossible on Pesach. However according to Tosafot daf 41 that even for Tanna Kama pot-roasting is invalid, and also there is a positive commandment that only fire-roasting applies, if so even if it deals with roasting in two pots he challenges Pesachim properly.
yad-ephraim/6:_: There subsection 29, and so appears the law in Be'er HaGolah: if so there is no proof to forbid kli sheini etc., for Be'er HaGolah wrote in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot etc., thus it should read — it appears to explain: granted if we say cold is entirely permitted, there is well proof from Mordechai regarding kli sheini, for although it deals with pouring water into the vessel and nevertheless it is kli sheini, it is implied it deals with placing the chicken afterward, or even if the chicken was there at scalding; nevertheless even though the bowl discharges because of iruy, this discharge has no power to return and be absorbed in the chicken, only because of the hot inside, and this is only kli sheini (and it appears this is the view of "there are those who permit" mentioned in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah end of siman 68: if they poured to scald a chicken in a milk pan — see there in Shach in the name of Levush who wrote the reason because the flow was interrupted; and in my humble opinion this is unnecessary, rather the reason is that the returned discharge that returns to absorb into the chicken again is not because of iruy but is like kli sheini, and Beit Yosef ruled there to permit in kli sheini); if so there is well proof from Mordechai regarding kli sheini, for although iruy acts regarding discharging the vessel, nevertheless regarding the chicken being forbidden there is only kli sheini, and it is proven that kli sheini forbids; not so if we say cold is forbidden, for since because of iruy the vessel discharged, automatically the chicken is forbidden even if only kli sheini — why would Rama forbid kli sheini when there is no gravy; and afterward he wrote "and furthermore Be'er HaGolah wrote" etc., and it should read that this is another gloss, meaning such is Darkei Moshe's view, which is another gloss, and therefore he wrote here two views in the gloss. And according to what was written above, for we can say Mordechai's reason there is discharge from the vessel through iruy and automatically the chicken is forbidden, not only cold; and what he wrote in the second gloss that in kli sheini one need not be concerned — meaning without gravy; and on this he wrote therefore it appears what Mordechai wrote to forbid in cold is because of filaments etc.; otherwise there is no prohibition in cold, if so there is well proof from Mordechai that even kli sheini is forbidden, for Mordechai forbids scalding the chicken even though the chicken is in its feathers and has no filaments, and iruy helps only to discharge from the vessel, as written; and see in my responsa Beit Efrayim Orach Chayim part siman 47, and there you will find this matter explained very much, and many were perplexed on this, and emended and switched the views, and the examiner will see that this explanation is correct and illuminates the eyes, with God's help.
yad-ephraim/7:_: There subsection 15, and as he wrote siman 467 seif 14 etc. — meaning there in subsection 33 he wrote that if the brine does not rise above it, it has the law of salting, and its law as Rama wrote in his responsum — see there, Magen Avraham hinted here; and regarding that piece itself, what is outside the brine — one can also say it is permitted, as Taz wrote siman 467 subsection 20; and although in other prohibitions we say perhaps it permeates upward, nevertheless in chametz which is a weak prohibition one need not be stringent; and see in Shach siman 105; and more plausible that Magen Avraham refers to what was written above in the name of Rama regarding soaking overnight, and there the law of salting does not apply at all, for water nullifies the power of the brine, only from the law of pickling it is forbidden; and then what is outside the brine was not softened and did not absorb at all; and elsewhere I elaborated on this on Avodah Zarah at the beginning of siman 105 in the name of Or Hashem, and what Magen Avraham wrote "and so Taz in Yoreh De'ah siman 83" — meaning there subsection 6, that we require the brine to rise above both of them, then it is like pickling when soaked overnight — see there; and what Magen Avraham wrote "and in Derishah siman 69 and in Beit Shmuel" etc., and in my humble opinion there is a missing word and it should read "and in Derishah siman 69 Derishah wrote that even for discharge from a vessel the law of pickling applies, and in Be'ur Sheva perek 25 Beit Shmuel wrote" etc., meaning Beit Shmuel holds the law of pickling does not help to discharge from a vessel; see Minchat Yaakov general rule 12 subsection 14.
yad-ephraim/9:_: Magen Avraham subsection 28: therefore if it stood before chametz etc. — see Chok Yaakov that even not ben yomo one should forbid since it is a sharp thing; and some emend in Magen Avraham "even not ben yomo"; and perhaps since it is not ben yomo and ta'am bar ta'am also, nevertheless many Poskim hold that pickling so that it is placed on fire etc. does not discharge from a vessel, as written in subsection 17 — one need not be stringent.
yad-ephraim/10:_: Taz subsection 14: in Tur it is written "and so it appears" from what Rosh wrote regarding an onion cut with a knife etc. — see Magen Avraham subsection 37 where it is explained that if they used the knife hot it would forbid.
yad-ephraim/11:_: Magen Avraham subsection 42: some say it is forbidden on Pesach as written subsection 14; nevertheless after Pesach it is nullified, thus it should read.
yad-ephraim/12:_: There: if there are not sixty one transgresses on it, and so Tur etc. — meaning Tur there wrote that if there is taste one is liable d'oraisa — see there in Magen Avraham subsection 1; and therefore he wrote that in min b'mino where there is no taste, if so one does not transgress on it, as also explained in that siman — permitted after Pesach if one retained it; but to mix and retain it, perhaps it is forbidden in Hagahot Maimoniyot, for even though everything one does not transgress d'oraisa from the Torah is permitted to mix and retain, this is specifically such as made for preservation and there is not in any case what is here that is less than sixty and against it in not its kind gives taste — therefore even though it is min b'mino it is forbidden to mix intentionally to retain, because of a decree lest one do so not in its kind; and he wrote perhaps therefore Mahari wrote that if one nullifies etc., for Tur challenged him: if it is a thing on which one transgresses d'oraisa, nullification does not help at all; and if one does not transgress, even to mix l'chatchila to retain is permitted; on this Magen Avraham wrote perhaps it deals in such a case where there is taste-giving amount, only it is min b'mino; and in such a case it is forbidden l'chatchila, as it appears to me; and see in siman 442 until "and if it became mixed less than a kezayit" etc. — these are not Bach's words but Magen Avraham's own words; and what he wrote "and if it became mixed" etc. — for this he intended in the gloss, it is from Bach who wrote that from Rama's language it is implied it deals even if he knew beforehand and transgressed and retained, redemption helps, and this means it deals when there is not a kezayit of chametz; not so Hagahot Maimoniyot who wrote we require it was not known, dealing when there is a kezayit of chametz from the chametz.
